intended_object: The coordinate ring of the standard affine chart D₊(Xᵢ) of the projective Weierstrass cubic W(X₀,X₁,X₂)=0 over a commutative ring R. It is presented as R[X₀,X₁,X₂]/(W, Xᵢ − 1), which is the dehomogenization isomorphic to the degree-zero localization A_(Xᵢ). This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body takes the quotient of `MvPolynomial (Fin 3) R` by the ideal spanned by `![W'.polynomial, X i - 1]`. Here `W'.polynomial` is Mathlib's homogeneous Weierstrass polynomial for the projective model. This is exactly R[X₀,X₁,X₂]/(W, Xᵢ − 1), as the docstring says.

Setting Xᵢ = 1 in the homogeneous cubic gives the dehomogenized affine equation. The resulting ring is isomorphic to the degree-zero part of the homogeneous coordinate ring localized at Xᵢ. That is the standard coordinate ring of the chart D₊(Xᵢ), and the file proves this isomorphism as `awayEquivChartRing`.

The definition works over any commutative ring R and for each of the three charts i, which is the natural generality for a Weierstrass curve. The only possible Mathlib counterpart is `WeierstrassCurve.Affine.CoordinateRing`. It covers only the Z = 1 chart and is presented with two variables, so it is not the same object in this uniform three-chart form.
